brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Lower storey pieces at level 0 (0,0 full, 1,0 full, 0,1 half-n) with journal pieces 0,0,1 and 1,0,1 at level 1 above them; check_build confirms 2 storey groups and meshClash clear.

bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-half-div2 (two compartments) and bin:1,0,1~hex-bin-half-div3 (three compartments) on the upper storey; dressed with a standing pen (prop:11) and marker (prop:12) that are visible from above and at polar 62.
drawer:0#0,1#cut on the cut face of the half-n base at 0,1, level 0.
capOpenFaces applied: 15 solid caps (cap:0,0,0, cap:0,0,1, cap:0,1,0, cap:1,0,0, cap:1,0,1); check_build reports no OPEN_CAP_FACE issues; lockJoints also applied (jointBolt at both storeys).

Bins show a pen and marker standing in them. Screw/nut heaps were tried but sit 44mm below the rim in every bin depth offered (PROP_BELOW_RIM), and tool sets were refused as too wide/would shift, so the fastener dressing was not kept.

finish.summary: Two-storey workbench organizer: a 3-cell lower storey (two full hex bases plus a north half-base) topped by two full bases forming the second storey. The upper cells carry a 2-compartment and a 3-compartment half-depth bin, dressed with a standing pen and marker. A classic drawer sits in the lower half-base's cut face. All 15 open faces are capped with solid end caps, joints are bolted, and check_build passes with meshClash clear (40 parts, ~2.37 kg print estimate). Parts settled on half-depth bins after the full-depth versions proved too deep for visible small-item dressing.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
